candidates.attacker_control: The entire 'Authorization: Digest ...' header is attacker-controlled: username, realm, nonce (including the base64-encoded 'expiry:signature' contents), uri, response, qop, nc and cnonce. Because the signature field of the nonce is never actually validated, an attacker can mint nonces without knowing the DigestAuthenticationEntryPoint key, including nonces whose first token is an arbitrary far-future expiry.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The check is not compensated elsewhere: 'expectedNonceSignature' appears only at this site (and in DigestAuthenticationEntryPointTests), and 'nonceCompromised' is only referenced here. The existing test testNonceWithIncorrectSignatureForNumericFieldReturnsForbidden (lines 240-256) does not catch the defect because its forged nonce uses '123456' as expiry, which is already in the past, so the separate expiry check rejects it. Other validations (mandatory fields, qop, realm equality, base64/format, expiry) are intact, and the response digest still depends on the user's password; this is not by itself an unauthenticated login bypass. The rest of the class otherwise matches later upstream structure (this is the only spot in the main sources where a *Exception(...) is constructed as a statement without 'throw').
candidates.impact: The nonce is not authenticated to the server, so the intended anti-replay/nonce-expiry policy of Digest authentication can be bypassed: attacker-chosen nonces with arbitrary (e.g. far-future) expiry are accepted. Combined with the fact that the header's uri (not the actual request URI) is what is hashed, this allows captured Digest Authorization headers to remain reusable well beyond the configured nonceValiditySeconds (default 300s) and weakens digest authentication to replayable credentials within the target realm. This only affects deployments that explicitly enable the legacy DigestAuthenticationFilter.
candidates.prerequisites: The application must use the legacy/deprecated DigestAuthenticationFilter for authentication (not a default). The attacker must be able to send a crafted Authorization header. To ultimately obtain an authenticated session the attacker must still produce a response digest that matches the server-computed value, i.e. a captured/derived digest response for the target method (for example by injecting a forged long-lived nonce into a victim's client via MITM and capturing the resulting response, or by knowing the credentials).
candidates.root_cause: In DigestAuthenticationFilter.DigestData.validateAndDecode, the nonce authenticity check computes expectedNonceSignature = md5Hex(nonceExpiryTime + ":" + entryPointKey) and compares it to the nonce's second token. When the comparison fails, the failure branch only instantiates a BadCredentialsException; it never throws it (no 'throw' keyword, and the return value is discarded). Execution therefore continues as if the nonce had been validated. Downstream, nonceExpiryTime comes from the attacker-supplied nonce itself, so the only remaining temporal control is the client-chosen expiry; the later response-digest comparison uses the same attacker-supplied header values (nonce, uri, qop, nc, cnonce) and the request method.
candidates.title: DigestAuthenticationFilter nonce-signature verification is a no-op (exception constructed but never thrown)
candidates.trace: DigestAuthenticationFilter.doFilter (line 118) reads the Authorization header, constructs DigestData and calls validateAndDecode(entryPointKey, realm) (line 139). validateAndDecode performs shape/realm/base64/expiry parsing, then at lines 430-435 detects an invalid nonce signature but only constructs BadCredentialsException without throwing, so it returns normally. The filter then computes serverDigestMd5 from the user's password and the header-supplied values (line 169/182, calculateServerDigest line 438-446) and accepts the request if it matches. Because isNonceExpired (line 448-451) reads the expiry embedded in the attacker-supplied nonce, a forged far-future nonce passes the only remaining time check, and createSuccessfulAuthentication sets the SecurityContextHolder with the target user's identity (lines 230-235).
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-verified. Whether this specific defect is the dataset's intended vulnerability, and whether/when upstream added the missing 'throw' (e.g. via a later release on the 4.2.x line), could not be confirmed from the snapshot alone; version dating inside the snapshot is ambiguous because gradle.properties (4.2.13.BUILD-SNAPSHOT) and some newer-looking backported files do not allow a precise commit date.
candidates.weakness_type: Improper Authentication / Failure of a security check (CWE-287; protection-mechanism failure)

coverage_summary: Relation scope reports 1,979 visible files (1,648 Java files parsed, 424 omitted/non-parsed), 15,342 symbols, 46,318 call sites and 30,257 edges, with control flow, data flow, semantic resolution and Spring runtime DI/security enforcement explicitly not implemented; the index is syntactic navigation evidence only. I used it to locate and then read source in the security-relevant areas: web filters (FilterChainProxy, ExceptionTranslationFilter, Firewall, CSRF, request cache/redirect strategies, session/context management, remember-me, Basic/Digest auth, login/logout, switch-user, matchers, servlet API wrappers), core authentication/authorization (ProviderManager, DaoAuthenticationProvider, UserDetails services, access voters, token service, SecureRandomFactoryBean), config (HttpSecurity configurers, RequestCacheConfigurer, authorization configurers), acl jdbc, crypto password/keygen, messaging matchers, test support (MockMvc post-processors/builders), openid, cas, and representative tests. Sampled/not exhaustively read: every file and every test, taglibs/aspects/remoting/data details, samples, and most docs/build config.
limitations: No runtime, build, test or scanner execution was performed; the candidate is a source-level lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.
The P1 index explicitly lacks control-flow, data-flow, semantic resolution and runtime reachability; only 1,648 of 1,980 files were parsed and 33,083 calls were unresolved.

Exact branch/commit dating is uncertain: gradle.properties says 4.2.13.BUILD-SNAPSHOT and module poms say 4.2.12.RELEASE, while a few files contain later-looking backports, so the specific upstream fix commit for VUL4J-73 could not be proven from the snapshot.
Not every security-relevant file was read line-by-line (e.g. large config, ldap, cas, openid, and test trees were sampled); other unconfirmed defects may exist.

The candidate's practical impact is bounded by the requirement to use DigestAuthenticationFilter and to obtain a matching digest response; only replay/lifetime and nonce-authenticity assurances are affected, not a direct unauthenticated login bypass.

rejected_leads.lead: DefaultLoginPageGeneratingFilter appends AuthenticationException#getMessage() into the generated HTML without escaping (web/.../ui/DefaultLoginPageGeneratingFilter.java lines 182-206), a potential reflected/stored XSS if a custom AuthenticationException carries attacker-controlled text.
rejected_leads.reason: Exception messages from standard DaoAuthenticationProvider paths are fixed strings ('Bad credentials'); exploitation needs a non-standard exception built from user input, and no corresponding validation/fix artifact is visible in this snapshot to support it as the intended issue.

The file already requests bytes before setSeed (the state-preserving fix), has a 2019 copyright, and its regression test SecureRandomFactoryBeanTests#testCreatesUsingSeed is present, so the snapshot appears to contain the fixed behavior.
Implementation matches the known hardened form (normalization, blacklisted encoded chars, printable-ASCII check); no concrete gap could be shown from source.

rejected_leads.lead: SQL injection in ACL/JDBC code (BasicLookupStrategy, JdbcAclService, JdbcMutableAclService) flagged by the relation index.
rejected_leads.reason: All queries use parameter placeholders/PreparedStatementSetter; the index hits are name-based hints only.
String equality on random tokens was not fixed as a security issue in this era and no fix artifact is present; kept as unconfirmed hardening observations.

rejected_leads.lead: DefaultLoginPageGeneratingFilter/LogoutFilter/OpenID/CAS redirects (sendRedirect sites flagged by the index).
rejected_leads.reason: Redirect targets are configuration values revalidated with UrlUtils.isValidRedirectUrl or are the configured identity-provider URL; no attacker-controlled redirect target was established.

summary: Snapshot is the Spring Security 4.2.x branch (gradle.properties 4.2.13.BUILD-SNAPSHOT, module poms 4.2.12.RELEASE) containing the 4.2-era modules (core, web, config, acl, ldap, cas, openid, crypto, messaging, test). I reviewed request matching/firewall, CSRF, session/context, remember-me, Basic/Digest authentication, form login, CVE-related paths, ACL/JDBC code and crypto helpers. The single strongest source-evidenced candidate is a dead security check in DigestAuthenticationFilter: the nonce-signature comparison computes an expected signature and, on mismatch, builds a BadCredentialsException without throwing it, so the check has no effect and attacker-influenced nonces are accepted (only the nonce's self-declared expiry is subsequently honored).
